title: No console logging in application source

facts.note: Any application source file, new or existing; test files and vendored/build directories are excluded by path.
A console.log/info/warn/error/debug/trace/dir call outside masked strings/comments, reported by bun_security_hygiene_detector.

fires: A server handler or service module in application source calls console.log/info/warn/error/debug/trace/dir.
A shared module that runs on both server and browser calls console.error in a catch block.
A CLI entry point in application source prints its user-facing output with console.log.
An existing application source file already contains a console.warn call.
doesNotFire: `console.log` appears only inside a comment or a string literal.
console.* calls in vendored or build output directories.
A CLI writes its user-facing output via process.stdout.write / process.stderr.write.

given: A Bun application source file (not a test, vendored or build file).
when: Code calls console.log/info/warn/error/debug/trace/dir, for any purpose (log, diagnostic or CLI interface output).
then: Do not call `console.log`/`info`/`warn`/`error`/`debug`/`trace`/`dir` in application source; log via the structured logger.
prefer: `logger.info("processing order", { orderId: order.id });` (the logger owns level, timestamp, correlation).
CLI whose stdout IS its UI: `process.stdout.write` (errors: `process.stderr.write`); it says it is the interface, not a log.
avoid: `console.log("processing", order.id);`; `console.error` too: stderr is still unlevelled, uncorrelated, not queryable.
Per-file exemptions (none exist); process.stdout.write for output that is really a log.
unless: Inside a comment or string literal (masked, never flagged).
why: console.* lacks level, timestamp and request correlation, so production logs become one unfilterable stream; a full-stack module may run in the browser, sending output to the user's devtools, not the operator.
evidence: bun_security_hygiene_detector reports no LOGGING-PRINT-001 finding across in-scope application source (not only changed files).
Review: log output goes through the structured logger (levels, timestamps, correlation); CLI interface output uses process.stdout.write / process.stderr.write.
verifier_detail: Detector: bun_security_hygiene_detector (validator), core alias LOGGING-PRINT-001. Matches calls to console.log, console.info, console.warn, console.error, console.debug, console.trace, console.dir.
Source is scanned with strings and comments MASKED, so `console.log` inside a comment or string literal never trips the rule.
Test files and vendored/build directories are excluded from the scan.
Only console.* is matched; process.stdout.write / process.stderr.write are not flagged. atdd-bun has no per-rule scope to exempt a file.
Term unlevelled_output: a console.* call — no level, no timestamp, no request correlation; in a full-stack app the same module may write to the operator's stdout or the user's devtools.
Term structured_logger: the project logger that owns levels, timestamps and correlation.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Stack-neutral obligation, RE-REALIZED for Bun: the python-pytest sibling walks the AST for a bare `print(...)`; the Bun equivalent is `console.*`.
The obligation is the same as the Python one but the consequence is sharper.

additions.text: fires/doesNotFire examples (shared server/browser module, CLI using console.log, existing file with console.warn).
additions.justification: Required activation examples; derived directly from source statement, reasoning and exceptions; no new obligation.

additions.text: process.stdout.write for output that is really a log rather than a CLI's interface.
additions.justification: Metric-gaming guard: the source permits process.stdout.write only because it 'says plainly that it is the interface, not a log'; this makes that limit explicit since the detector matches only console.*.
